summary: Every legal input is disproved by one fixed-form witness base, so no input-sized workload remains to scale and the constant-time upper bound matches the unavoidable constant decision cost.

optimality.argument: Any implementation must produce one boolean decision. For n greater than 4, base n - 2 represents n as the unequal digits 12; for n equal to 4, base 2 represents it as 100. Returning false therefore uses a fixed amount of work and matches the Omega(1) lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: A correct call must emit one boolean result, which requires Omega(1) work.
The accepted reference returns false directly after the universal base n - 2 counterexample proves the result for the whole legal domain.
Regression checks every integer from 4 through 100000, verifies the explicit witness digits, and independently brute-converts every required base for small inputs.
